title_en: The ETF Stories to Watch for the Rest of 2026
title_zh: 2026年剩余时间值得关注的ETF故事 | Cynthia Murphy、Jeff Klingelhofer
subtitle_zh: 盘点351条交换新规、新型ETF、体育期货、德州交易所与资金流纪录，并对话Aristotle太平洋三只主动固收ETF。
description: The ETF Stories to Watch for the Rest of 2026

turns.en: This is a warning. It's not any kind of regulatory enforcement right now, but it's definitely a red flag for this path to ETFs that we've seen really get popular in recent years.

turns.en: All right, joining me will be Jeff Klingelhofer, managing director and portfolio manager at Aristotle Pacific, who entered the ETF space a little over two months ago with a launch of three actively managed fixed income ETFs. These cover core plus multi sector and short term income. And I should note that Aristotle Pacific is a 31 billion dollar asset manager overall. And so we're going to find out why they decided to
turns.zh: 好的，稍后会加入节目的是Aristotle Pacific的董事总经理兼投资组合经理Jeff Klingelhofer。两个多月前，他们通过发行三只主动管理型固定收益ETF正式进军ETF领域，分别覆盖核心增强（core plus）、多行业和短期收益策略。需要说明的是，Aristotle Pacific整体是一家管理310亿美元的资管机构。我们会请他谈谈为什么决定……

turns.en: enter the ETF space. Now, what the decision making was behind that will obviously spotlight those three ETFs. And then we're going to spend a decent amount of time just getting into the current fixed income market environment. Jeff is someone who's been involved in this asset class for over two decades. So prior to Aristotle, he was at PIMCO and Thornburg. And so he has certainly seen a thing or two in fixed income. And I thought
turns.zh: ……进军ETF领域。当然，讲完这个决策过程，我们自然会聚焦那三只ETF，然后花相当多的时间讨论当前的固收市场环境。Jeff在这个资产类别里已经深耕二十多年，来Aristotle之前他在PIMCO和Thornburg工作过，在固收领域绝对见过大场面。我想，

turns.en: given everything going on right now, especially with interest rates, it'd be interesting to hear how he's viewing duration risk, inflation and how the Fed is handling everything. So he'll join me a bit later to do that. Now to start this week, I'll be joined by Cynthia Murphy, director of research at vetify. And as we enter the fourth quarter, Cynthia and I thought it might be fun to look at some of the big ETF stories
turns.zh: 鉴于眼下发生的一切，尤其是利率环境，很想听听他如何看待久期风险（duration risk）、通胀，以及美联储的应对。这部分他稍后会来聊。本周开场，我先请到了VettaFi的研究总监Cynthia Murphy。进入第四季度，Cynthia和我觉得不妨一起回顾一下我们在今年剩余时间重点关注的几个大ETF故事。

turns.en: we're watching for the remainder of the year. And I would say many of these we have certainly covered and at least some capacity throughout the first three quarters. But we both think these are all noteworthy to keep tracking as we close out 2026 and really into 2027. And so we'll get into those here in just a moment. As always, questions or comments you can find me on x at Nate Geracy, or you can go to etfprime.com. So let me first
turns.zh: 其中很多故事在前三个季度我们多少都报道过，但我们俩都认为，在收官2026年、乃至延伸到2027年的过程中，这些值得持续跟踪。一会儿我们就展开。照例，有任何问题或意见，可以在X上找我：Nate Geraci，或者访问etfprime.com。那我先……

turns.en: welcome in vetify Cynthia Murphy, who is joining me from the vetify New York studio. Cynthia, always great having you on here. Hey, Nate excited to be here and today with great video quality, which is not the usual for me.
turns.zh: ……欢迎VettaFi的Cynthia Murphy，她正在VettaFi纽约演播室和我连线。Cynthia，每次请你上节目都很开心。嗨，Nate，很高兴来到这里，而且今天视频质量特别好，这对我来说可不常见。

turns.en: I love it. You look great. You sound great. And this is going to be a fun discussion. I think we have six or seven ETF stories to go through here, though. I was thinking about this, we could probably come up with like 20 stories, because it's been a pretty wild year in ETF. So I guess as we both like to refer to it as job security, right?
turns.zh: 太棒了。你看起来状态很好，声音也很棒。我们今天肯定聊得很有意思。我想大概有六七个ETF故事要过一遍。不过我刚才还在想，我们其实能列出20个故事，因为今年ETF行业实在太热闹了。所以就像我们俩爱说的那样，这就是职业安全感（job security），对吧？

turns.en: Keeps us busy. That's for sure. So let's start with probably the biggest story, certainly from last week, maybe over the past several weeks, which was the Treasury Department issuing what all a very loosely called guidance. I have my air quotes up on 351 exchanges. Of course, 351 exchanges, those have really grown in popularity. I think there are now over 100 ETFs with some 20 to 25 billion dollars
turns.zh: 确实让我们很忙。那我们就从可能最大的故事聊起——肯定算上周、乃至过去几周最重要的一条新闻：财政部发布了宽泛意义上的所谓指引。我这里要打上双引号——关于351条交换（Section 351 exchange）。当然，351条交换这些年真的越来越流行。我想现在已经有超过100只ETF、大约200亿到250亿美元的资金……

turns.en: that were seeded via a 351 exchange. And I should say up front, by the way, Cynthia, neither you nor I are tax experts. So I want to be very clear on that. But the gist of the guidance is that the IRS is apparently cracking down on 351 exchanges that they view as quote unquote, abusive. And real quick, for people not familiar with 351 exchanges, at a very basic level, these allow an investor to contribute
turns.zh: ……是通过351条交换种子化设立的。我得先把话说在前面，Cynthia，你和我都不是税务专家，这一点我要讲清楚。但这份指引的要旨是：国税局（IRS）显然正在打击那些他们所谓'滥用'的351条交换。快速给不熟悉351条交换的朋友解释一下：最基本地讲，它允许投资者把……

turns.en: individual stocks or other securities into an ETF and receive ETF shares in return. And the key here is if this is done correctly, this is not a taxable event. Now, the reason you might do this is say you own a fairly concentrated portfolio of individual stocks that have gone up a lot in value, and maybe you would rather have more diversification. Well, if you were to sell those stocks, you're gonna have to pay capital
turns.zh: ……个股或其他证券注入一只ETF，作为对价收到ETF份额。关键在于，如果操作得当，这不构成应税事件。你为什么可能这么做呢？比如你持有一个相当集中的个股组合，这些股票涨了很多，而你也许更想要分散化。如果你直接卖掉这些股票，你就得缴纳资本利得税。

turns.en: gains tax. But instead, if you contribute them into an ETF, you can now own ETF shares, you gain that diversification, you get the tax efficiency of the ETF wrapper and all the other benefits of the ETF wrapper. And so there are some clear benefits here. However, now, the Treasury Department is apparently cracking down on these, at least to some degree.
turns.zh: 但如果你把它们注入ETF，你就持有了ETF份额，获得了分散化，享受ETF载体（wrapper）的税务效率以及它的所有其他好处。所以这里面确实有明显的益处。不过现在，财政部显然至少在某种程度上开始打击这类操作。

turns.en: And so to start here, Cynthia, what did you make of all this? So I think what's interesting here, first of all, to reinforce what you just said, Nate, this is a warning, it's not any kind of regulatory enforcement right now. But it's definitely a red flag for this path to ETFs that we've seen really get popular in recent years. What's interesting is is I mean, we know the government doesn't mess with taxes, right?
turns.zh: 所以Cynthia，我们先从这里开始，你怎么看这件事？我觉得有意思的是——首先要强化你刚才说的，Nate——这是一次警告，眼下还算不上任何监管执法。但对近年来真正火起来的这条进入ETF的路径来说，这绝对是一个危险信号。有意思的是，我们都知道，政府是不会在税收上开玩笑的，对吧？

turns.en: So here we have the beauty of this, you know, section 351 code part of the tax code that allows you to transfer property to a corporation in exchange for shares and not realize a capital gain in that transaction, which became a beautiful way to just pull different investors from different places with different amount of shares in different companies. Like we see this used a lot by high net worth individuals or folks who have a lot of their own
turns.zh: 所以我们看到的是这个机制的精妙之处——税法里的第351条，允许你把资产转让给公司换取股份，而不用在这笔交易中确认资本利得。它变成了一种很美妙的方式，把来自不同地方、在不同公司持有不同数量股票的投资者聚合起来。我们看到很多高净值人士，或者持有大量自家股票的人——比如在自己的公司工作之类的——

turns.en: company stock or they work or things like that. And then you pull these investors together and create an ETF of all these shares together, there's limitations on exposure or on concentration, all those those sorts of things. But the point is, you don't have to realize those capital gains in that transaction. And then the ETF through the beautiful creation redemption mechanism, and work on that, you know, cost
turns.zh: 大量使用这种方式。然后把这些投资者拉到一起，用所有这些股票组建一只ETF。在敞口或集中度上有限制，各种此类规定。但关键是，你不用在这笔交易中确认那些资本利得。然后ETF通过精妙的申赎机制去处理成本基础（cost basis），实现真正的高税务效率。

turns.en: basis, and be really tax efficient. Now, the whole process while beautiful, it's a tax deferral effort. According to the IRS and the Treasury, they're seeing this now as a tax dodge, which they don't don't like, right? So I think it's, we maybe we're getting too clever for ourselves. And that's what happens, you find a loophole and you just, you know, bulldozer through it. Is this going to impact, I think, the ETF space?
turns.zh: 而整个过程虽然精妙，本质上是一个税务递延的安排。在国税局和财政部看来，他们现在把这当成逃税避税，而他们不喜欢这样，对吧？所以我觉得，也许是我们聪明反被聪明误了。就是这样，你找到一个漏洞，然后开着推土机直接碾过去。我想这会不会影响ETF领域？

turns.en: I think you definitely slowed down 351s. I saw a data point from Bloomberg, that we've had already about $22 billion of ETFs that have come through 351 exchanges, which have basically meant about six and a half billion dollars in unrealized cap gains taxes there. So it's big numbers. I think this will mean now that we know the Treasury is watching, maybe we'll be more thoughtful. But I'm sure you saw this too,
turns.zh: 我认为351条交换肯定会慢下来。我看到彭博的一个数据点：已经大约有220亿美元的ETF是通过351条交换设立的，这背后大致相当于65亿美元的未实现资本利得税。数字很大。我觉得，既然现在知道财政部在盯着，也许大家会更审慎。我相信你也看到了，

turns.en: Nate, the concern isn't about folks using 351 exchanges as design, is folks abusing through 51 exchanges, doing things like unloading your stock and then quickly redeeming on the other side, or you unload on one type of ETF and then ETF overnight becomes a completely different fund. So things that suggest this wasn't intended as a tax efficiency move, it really is intended of getting out of taxes completely. So, you
turns.zh: Nate，问题不在于人们按设计初衷使用351条交换，而在于有人滥用351条交换，比如甩掉自己的股票，然后在另一边快速赎回；或者你调入一种ETF，结果这只ETF一夜之间变成完全不同的基金。这些都说明它压根不是出于税务效率的考虑，而是纯粹想彻底摆脱税负。所以，

turns.en: know, this is what happens when I guess we get too clever. All of that is extremely well stated, a few things that I'll add. First of all, I do think it's important to note that this isn't a tax avoidance strategy per se, this is a tax deferral, and you see some of the headlines out there, I even use, you know, the air quotes around abusive. I think we have to be careful with that. I mean, this is a deferral strategy. And I think
turns.zh: 我想说，这就是我们太聪明的下场。以上说得非常好，我补充几点。首先，我确实认为重要的是要指出，这本身并不是一个税务规避策略，而是税务递延。你看外面的一些标题，我自己也用了'滥用'这个词，还打上双引号——我觉得我们得小心措辞。这是一个递延策略。我认为……

turns.en: to what you were saying, I think the key here is, if somebody comes in with a plan to take a highly concentrated portfolio, let's say of US stocks, in my example, and contribute those to the ETF and the ETF very quickly purges those via the redemption process, and they have a very different portfolio.
turns.zh: ……承接你刚才说的，我觉得关键在于：如果有人带着这样的计划进来——拿一个高度集中的美股组合，比如我举的这个例子，注入ETF，而ETF又非常快地通过赎回程序把这些股票清掉，最后手里是一个非常不同的组合。

turns.en: So maybe we went from a US centric individual stock portfolio to let's say an international ETF. Well, that's something that the IRS is going to take a look at. But I think what is a little bit of a challenge here is if, and I can't say I read through every single word of the guidance they put out, there's a lot of gray area here. And I think it's going to be very difficult for some of the opera, the ETF
turns.zh: 也许我们就从一个以美股为主的个股组合变成了一个国际ETF，那这就是国税局要盯着看的情形。但我觉得有些挑战在于——我没法说我逐字逐句读完了他们发布的指引——这里面有很大的灰色地带。我认为这对一些ETF……

turns.en: operators in this space to figure out where the boundaries are. Because of that, I think, you said this, I think we are going to see a slowdown in 351 exchanges, at least here in the short term, while issuers evaluate this guidance, and consult with tax counsel, probably legal counsel to make sure they're crossing all their T's and nodding all their eyes. You know, some of the other things that I've seen out
turns.zh: ……的运作方来说，要搞清楚边界在哪里会非常困难。正因如此，我想你也说过，我们预计351条交换会慢下来，至少在短期内，发行商需要评估这份指引，咨询税务顾问，可能还有法律顾问，确保每个细节都滴水不漏。关于这个话题，我在外面看到的其他一些说法是……

turns.en: here on this is, you know, the high net worth community has been using strategies like this forever. And now that they've been put into a wrapper where anybody can access them, all the sudden, we have to, you know, take a magnifying glass here.
turns.zh: 高净值人群其实一直都在用这类策略。而现在这些策略被装进了一个谁都能参与的载体里，突然之间，我们就得拿放大镜来审视它了。

turns.en: And I have a little bit of an issue with that, though, I will say probably a lot of investors who are currently using 351 exchanges probably veer on the on the wealthy side, in general.
turns.zh: 对这一点我多少有点保留意见。当然我会说，目前使用351条交换的投资者，总体上大概率都偏富裕那一侧。

turns.en: But, you know, it's we're democratizing this type of this type of tax strategy. And now all of a sudden, we have the treasuring the IRS looking at it. So I don't know, we'll see. I definitely think this is a story to keep an eye on moving forward because as you mentioned, there's that 22 billion in assets that have come into these products. I said this was going to be one of the biggest stories of the year last year. And of course, it did
turns.zh: 但我们实际上是在让这类税务策略走向平民化，结果一夜之间，财政部和国税局开始盯着它了。所以我也说不好，走一步看一步。我绝对认为这是未来需要持续关注的故事，因为正如你所说，已经有220亿美元的资金流入了这些产品。我去年就说过这会是一年最大的故事之一，而它当然也确实成了。

turns.en: become that. So this is just an interesting one. I don't know if there's anything else you want to add before we move on. No, I was just going to say which with something I agree with you completely, which is actually a good thing, which is the minute it becomes an ETF story. I mean, it becomes a big story.
turns.zh: 所以这真的是个很有意思的故事。在进入下一个话题之前，看看你还有没有要补充的。没有，我只是想说一点我完全同意你的：这其实是件好事——一件事一旦成为ETF的故事，它就会变成大新闻。

turns.en: Talk about the power of the ETF, the power of the tech sufficiency and ETF, the creation, redeem process, all of those things. All of a sudden, any little movement in ETFs becomes a huge movement because the demand for ETFs is so large.
turns.zh: 这恰恰说明了ETF的力量：ETF税务效率的力量，申赎机制，所有这一切。突然间，ETF里的任何小动静都会变成大动静，因为对ETF的需求实在太大了。

turns.en: So that's the good side of the story. You know, the demand for this approach has been really big, like many other approaches, because everyone wants ETFs. So that's cool.
turns.zh: 所以这是故事的正面。这种方式的需求真的很大，就像很多其他创新一样，因为人人都想要ETF。这挺好的。

turns.en: Yeah, and we know the government is looking for revenue where they can find it, given our fiscal situation. So they're looking everywhere now, apparently. Okay, the next story we're watching in the fourth quarter is novel ETFs. And so back in, I believe it was the end of June, early July, the SEC requested public comment on novel ETFs. This was following a bunch of filings for prediction market ETFs. Though this request for
turns.zh: 是啊，而且我们知道，在我们这样的财政状况下，政府正在到处找收入来源，所以现在显然哪儿都在查。好，我们第四季度关注的下一个故事是新型ETF（novel ETFs）。回到我记得是六月底、七月初的时候，SEC就新型ETF征求公众意见。那是在一大批预测市场ETF申报之后。不过这次征求……

turns.en: comment pertain to any type of novel ETF, whether we're talking crypto ETFs, leverage products, private assets, etc. And essentially, the SEC was seeking feedback on how these ETFs come to market. So everything from whether they should be regulated under the Investment Company Act, to what the approval process should look like, to the possibility of confidential ETF filings, which I thought was interesting,
turns.zh: ……意见涵盖了所有类型的新型ETF，无论是加密ETF、杠杆产品还是私募资产等等。本质上，SEC是在征集关于这些ETF如何进入市场的反馈：从是否应受《投资公司法》（Investment Company Act）监管，到审批流程应该长什么样，再到保密申报ETF的可能性——我觉得这点很有意思。

turns.en: there was a lot here. But now that that formal public comment period has closed. And so we're all kind of just sitting here waiting to see what happens. Anything that you would add to that, Cynthia, I mean, I have this here, just it's certainly a story to watch because again, that public comment very close, we want to see what the SEC is going to do next.
turns.zh: 这里面内容很多。现在正式的公众征求意见期已经结束，我们大家都在等，看接下来会发生什么。Cynthia，对此你有什么要补充的吗？我的意思是，这当然是一个值得关注的故事，因为公众意见期刚刚结束，我们想知道SEC下一步会做什么。

turns.en: Yeah, so my a couple of thoughts, I think is really interesting that this public comment phase, it's a little bit of giving us room to self regulate, right? What kind of regulation do you want to see? What kind of who should be the boss here? What should be the restrictions? How should all this go down as we, you know, go into new territory with ETFs like prediction market ETFs, for example, be first of a kind,
turns.zh: 好的，我有几点想法。我觉得这次公众意见期特别有意思的地方在于，它某种程度上是给了我们自我规范的空间，对吧？你们希望看到什么样的监管？谁该当这个'老板'？应该有哪些限制？当我们进入像预测市场ETF这样的新领地、做第一批吃螃蟹的产品时，这一切该怎么走？

turns.en: all that stuff. So I think that's interesting. I mean, if you ask me my expectation, my expectation is that approval will follow. I don't think we've seen a lot of resistance in any other part of it. I mean, we just saw last week, the 3x commodity trusts approved including crypto, gold, oil and gas. And that approval came, I think took less than two months since Siebel filed for that relief request. So I think
turns.zh: 诸如此类的问题。所以我觉得这很有意思。要问我的预期，我的预期是批准会到来。我不觉得其他环节遇到了太多阻力。上周我们刚看到3倍杠杆商品信托（3x commodity trusts）获批，包括加密、黄金、石油和天然气。而那次审批，我记得从提交该豁免申请到获批不到两个月。所以我觉得……

turns.en: we are going to end up seeing these products come to market. And, you know, should they should they not is a different question. But I think it's definitely something we're going to be watching for in the last quarter.
turns.zh: 我们最终会看到这些产品进入市场。至于该不该让它们进来，那是另一个问题。但我认为这绝对是我们在最后一个季度要持续观察的事情。

turns.en: Sort of the main headline here is that ETF industry innovation is outpaced regulators ability to keep up with that innovation. And so I think this request for a public comment from the SEC was in response with that, like how do we deal with all of this innovation? And I didn't read through every single public comment that came back to the SEC. But from what I saw, a lot of these actually said, you know what, the way we're handling
turns.zh: 这里的主线其实是：ETF行业的创新速度已经超过了监管者跟得上的能力。所以我觉得SEC这次征求公众意见正是对这一点的回应——我们该如何应对这么多创新？我没有把每一份递交给SEC的公众意见都读完，但据我所见，很多意见其实是在说：我们现在的处理方式……

turns.en: things right now is perfectly fine overall. And so I don't know that we are going to see a whole lot of changes here. And I think you're right, I think we're going to start seeing these different products start coming to market. And I should know by the way, next Tuesday, potential special guest. So as long as his schedule allows, I'm actually going to be joined on here by Brian Daley, who's director of the Division of Investment

And I think you see that in the performance for our longer term strategies.
turns.zh: 但同时也让我们能问：这些机会里哪个能在下行中保护组合？我们出发点不是怎么抓更高收益，而是怎么做好下行保护，用世界其他地方没在看的方式去看每一个机会。这就是我们差异化的核心。我想在我们长期策略的业绩中也能看到这一点。

turns.en: Sort of on this topic of just differentiating or standing out in the crowd, I bear with me, I have to ask you the cliche question of why go active in fixed income, because something like 40% of those 1000 plus fixed income ETFs I mentioned, are passive. And as you know, many of those are extremely popular if you just look at the total assets in them. So for investors looking to allocate here, why consider active
turns.zh: 说到差异化、在芸芸中脱颖而出——请容我问那个老掉牙的问题：固收为什么要做主动？因为我刚才说的那1000多只固收ETF里，大概40%是被动。你也知道，光看资产规模，很多被动产品极其受欢迎。对想配置这块的投资者来说，为什么要考虑主动管理？

turns.en: management? You know, I think the way that I like to talk about the active versus passive debate is really, what are you trying to accomplish? Because I think we can agree, a passive strategy is just trying to look like a benchmark, it might be trying to slightly beat that benchmark. But its outcome is the benchmark.
turns.zh: 我谈主动对被动之争，喜欢回到一个根本问题：你想实现什么？因为我觉得我们都能同意，被动策略就是力求长得像一个基准，也许略赢一点，但它的结果就是基准。

turns.en: And so then the question becomes, well, what is the benchmark trying to do? And it's just a set of rules. In most case, they're incredibly static, right? So if we take the Barclays Ag, there's a set of rules, it doesn't matter what you or the investor are trying to do or what me, the asset manager is trying to do. It just says, All right, I'm just going to buy, you know, everything the US Treasury is issuing everything
turns.zh: 那么问题变成：基准想干嘛？它只是一套规则，而且大多极其静态。拿Barclays Ag来说，它有一套规则，不管投资者你想什么，也不管我这个资管方想什么，它只说：好，美国财政部发什么我买什么，机构按揭市场的所有东西，投资级公司债里符合某些规则的一切。

turns.en: in the agency mortgage market, everything that fits certain rules within the IG corporate space. And I don't care what the duration is, I don't care what the mix of quality, what sectors all of those things are. And so it's fine from a beta perspective, but it doesn't have an outcome in mind. And so we go back to when I was talking about the strategies, to me, really the reason to go active is to say, I have a portfolio, I have life
turns.zh: 我才不管久期是多少，不管质量结构、行业分布如何。从beta的角度这没问题，但它心里没有一个'结果'。所以回到我讲策略时的话：对我来说，做主动的真正理由是——我有一个组合，我有人生目标，我知道生活中可能冒出各种事情，我要的资产要契合我的情况，

turns.en: goals, right? I know various things that might be coming up. And I want an asset that's going to fit my situation and be complementary to everything else that I hold. And so really, the outcome to me is the biggest differentiator between active versus passive that as an active manager, I'm trying to deliver an outcome. Yes, I'm trying to beat a benchmark, but I'm really focused on that outcome. The second thing is I would say
turns.zh: 和我持有的其他东西形成互补。所以真正重要的是结果：对我来说，结果导向是主动和被动之间最大的差别——作为主动经理，我要交付一个结果。是的，我也想在基准上胜出，但我真正聚焦的是那个结果。第二点，我想说……

turns.en: is, you know, things like the Barclays ag just, they don't access a lot of parts of the market. And so if you kind of ignore all the shifts that have happened in the world, and you don't want to look at the other 50% of available opportunities, that's okay. But but really, it opens that relative value lens.
turns.zh: 是，像Barclays Ag这样的东西根本覆盖不到市场的很多角落。如果你无视世界已经发生的种种变化，不想去看另外那50%的可用机会，那也行。但主动打开的正是那副相对价值的眼镜，

turns.en: And I think results in potentially better outcomes for manager that knows how to access them. Something I've mentioned multiple times over the years on this podcast, but I'm actually really interested to hear your take on this is I've said for a long time that for whatever reason, investors and advisors seem much more comfortable navigating the equity space on their own versus fixed income. And so because of
turns.zh: 我认为，对于懂得怎么参与的经理，这有可能带来更好的结果。这些年我在这个播客里提过很多次，我倒很想听听你的看法：我长期认为，不知为何，投资者和顾问自己驾驭股票市场似乎比驾驭固收自如得多。正因如此，

turns.en: that, I do think they're much more inclined to use active management on fixed income. Because, again, for whatever reason, the knowledge, the expertise just isn't quite as deep there. And now, and we'll get into this in a moment with how challenging the fixed income environment is, I think that's making this even more pronounced this interest around active management, I'm assuming you would agree with that.
turns.zh: 我确实觉得他们在固收上更愿意用主动管理。因为同样不知为何，人们在固收上的知识、专业深度没那么够。而且眼下固收环境如此有挑战——我们一会儿就展开——我觉得这更放大了大家对主动管理的兴趣。我猜你也会同意。

turns.en: I certainly agree with it. And we can talk, you know, real quick, just kind of one data point that's a highly topical today, the world of AI and data centers, right, a huge amount of what's powering the US economy is the growth of data centers. And a lot of these data centers are coming in unique forms, they're not being issued specifically by the medids or Microsoft's or anthropics of the world, they're being issued
turns.zh: 我非常同意。我们可以快速说一个今天特别应景的数据点：AI和数据中心的世界。驱动美国经济的很大一块是数据中心的增长。而很多数据中心是以很特别的形式融资的，不是Meta、微软或者Anthropic这些公司直接发债，而是在表外，

turns.en: off balance sheet in a very kind of unique vehicle. And those things aren't finding their way into the index, they're just completely excluded. The index just says they put blinders on they say they don't exist. And therefore, if you're passive, it's not an opportunity. Now, some people may feel like it's a great opportunity, some folks may want to avoid them. But to me, it's important to say the complexity of the world is
turns.zh: 用非常独特的载体发行。这些东西完全进不了指数，被彻底排除在外。指数相当于戴上眼罩说：它们不存在。所以如果你是被动策略，这就不是一个机会。也许有人觉得这是个好机会，有人想躲开。但在我看来，重要的是承认世界的复杂性已经大大增加了。

turns.en: massively larger. The world of securitized products that are coming out all sorts of cash flows are being securitized and issued to investors, it's important to include those in that relative value lens, rather than just to ignore them. And so, yes, the complexity is tremendously higher. There are hundreds of thousands of things that a fixed income investor needs to look at versus maybe thousands at most on the equity
turns.zh: 证券化产品的世界里，各种现金流都被打包证券化卖给投资者，把这些纳入相对价值的视野很重要，而不是无视它们。没错，复杂程度高得多：固收投资者要看的是几十万个标的，而股票那边可能顶多几千个。

turns.en: side. And so it really is just a different universe. And I think that also makes fixed income much more important to look at from an active lens.
turns.zh: 所以这真的是一个完全不同的宇宙。也正因为如此，我认为固收尤其需要用主动的视角去看。

turns.en: Alright, so this is a good segue here. Let's get into the current fixed income markets and some of the challenges that investors and advisors are facing. And we talked about duration risk earlier, Jeff, I'll tell you, I have been surprised to watch investors pile into some of the longer duration treasury ETFs over the past five or six years. So there's actually a 20 plus year treasury ETF that everybody
turns.zh: 好，这是个很自然的过渡。我们来谈谈当前的固收市场，以及投资者和顾问正面临的一些挑战。刚才我们聊到久期风险。Jeff，说实话，过去五六年我看着投资者蜂拥进一些长久期国债ETF，是一直挺惊讶的。有一只大家熟知的20年以上期国债ETF，

turns.en: knows that's still in a 45% drawdown 45% drawdown since 2020. And listen to this, you probably already know this this stat, but it's taken in about $50 billion in new money over that time. It's amazing. But all that said, there does seem to be a lot more chatter now that maybe it is the right time to extend duration. So I'd love to hear how you're thinking about this.
turns.zh: 至今还在45%的回撤里——自2020年以来回撤45%。而且你听听这个，你可能早知道这个数据：这段时间它居然还吸入了约500亿美元的新钱。太惊人了。但话虽如此，现在确实有更多声音在说，也许正是拉长久期的时候了。很想听听你怎么看这件事。

turns.en: It really is the elephant in the room, right? And look, what I want to do is maybe take a quick journey. For many folks listening to this, and for most investors out there, our entire investing experience is defined by what is not a normal history, right? We weren't supposed to have interest rates suppressed at 0%. We weren't supposed to have all sorts of funky monetary policy with controlling the shape of the
turns.zh: 这确实是房间里的大象。我想先带大家快速回顾一下：对很多正在听的听众、对大多数投资者来说，我们整个投资经历是由一段不正常的历史定义的。我们本不该看到利率被压在0%，本不该看到各种花样的货币政策去控制收益率曲线的形状——QE1、QE2时代。

turns.en: yield curve in QE1 and QE2. And really, we have to remind ourselves that the journey to get there to low interest rates was great for bonds. But as we normalize on the other side, that journey has been very painful. And so I think where we are is entering a world today. And the way I like to talk about is now the right time to step into duration is go back to the outcome that you're trying to achieve, right? Think about fixed
turns.zh: 我们得提醒自己：通往低利率的那段路对债券很好。但当我们在另一侧回归正常时，那段路变得非常痛苦。所以现在，要问是不是入场久期的合适时机，我喜欢的回答方式是：回到你想实现的结果。把固收看成美国经济调控机制里的第一根杠杆。

turns.en: income as kind of being that first lever within the control mechanism for the US economy. If something costs more for me to buy, not just in price, but the next derivative, if I have to finance it, then I'm going to buy less of it. And so overall, it's this mechanism to control that supply demand balance. And where we find ourselves today is that rates have normalized, I would argue they're not going to go tremendously higher today.
turns.zh: 如果一样东西买起来更贵了——不只是价格，还有我要为它支付的融资成本——那我就会少买。所以总体而言，这是控制供需平衡的机制。我们今天所处的位置是：利率已经正常化。我认为，利率不会再大幅往上走。

turns.en: But importantly, and this is really the crux of it, is if the world becomes a less safe place, if we get a geopolitical shock, if we get a recession, if we get a classic business cycle, the Fed can cut rates. And when the Fed can cut rates, all of a sudden, right, that's that ballast that protection to your portfolio that matters so much when you're thinking about it from an outcome versus a benchmark. And so it's kind of
turns.zh: 但关键在于：如果世界变得更不安全，如果出现地缘政治冲击、衰退或者经典的经济周期，美联储就能降息。而美联储能降息，突然间就有了压舱石，有了组合的保护。当你从结果而非基准来思考时，这一点极其重要。所以这一切，把我们谈过的很多事情都串起来了。

turns.en: all these things we've already talked about kind of coming back together. But I think the starting place yields are back, I think they're tremendously interesting. There is an alternative to equity returns, you're able to get 7% yields in multi sector portfolios, mid sixes and core plus portfolios. That all of a sudden to me is tremendously, tremendously interesting on a standalone basis. But really,
turns.zh: 但起点在于：收益率回来了，我认为它们极其可观。股票回报之外终于有了替代品：多行业组合能拿到7%的收益，核心增强组合有6%中段。单看这一点，我觉得就已经足够足够吸引人了。但真正最有意思的是，

turns.en: what's most interesting is the ability for it to protect if and when equities maybe aren't working right in a slower state of the economy. And I think all that makes perfect sense. It gets back to bonds being a ballast in a portfolio that if we do have some sort of economic downturn, you mentioned geopolitical event that you have that counterbalance to your equity position. But let me ask you this. If you look at the longer
turns.zh: 当股票在经济放缓时也许失灵的情况下，它能提供保护。我觉得这些都很有道理，又回到了债券作为组合压舱石的角色：万一真的出现某种经济下行，或者你提到的地缘政治事件，你就有了一个对冲股票头寸的平衡力量。不过让我问你：如果看曲线的长端，

turns.en: end of the curve, obviously, inflation concerns have been driving up rates. I think there are a lot of investors who are worried about the country's debt situation right now over $40 trillion in debt. We now have Treasury Secretary Scott Besson ramping up longer dated bond purchases, which that actually seemed to spook some investors versus helping the situation. And then I think the other factor here, you were mentioning AI
turns.zh: 显然通胀担忧一直在推高利率。我想很多投资者正担心国家的债务状况——现在债务已经超过40万亿美元。财政部长Scott Bessent还加大了长期债券的购买，而这反而似乎吓到了部分投资者，没有改善局面。我觉得另一个因素，你刚才提到AI数据中心——

turns.en: data centers earlier, you're having a lot of debt issuance from AI data centers, which is theoretically sapping some demand away from, from longer dated treasuries. And you can pick whatever yield you want to look at. But I was looking at the 30 year yield, that's up about a full percentage point since February. And you mentioned earlier that I think your bias is that you don't think rates have much more room to the upside.
turns.zh: AI数据中心发了大量债务，理论上会分走长端国债的一部分需求。你可以看任何一段收益率，但我看了30年期收益率，自2月以来已经上行约一个百分点。你前面提到过，我理解你的倾向性判断是利率上行空间不大了。当然，我们谁都没有水晶球，

turns.en: And admittedly, none of us have a crystal ball, I think you would say the same thing. But my question to you is, what actually changes the trajectory that we have seen here recently, what maybe gets rates coming back the other way, outside of an economic downturn or some major geopolitical event?
turns.zh: 我想你也会这么说。但我的问题是：除了经济衰退或者重大地缘政治事件之外，究竟什么才能改变我们最近看到的这条轨迹，让利率朝反方向走？

turns.en: Well, I think those last two are actually important, and I'll come back to them. But let's just start with kind of the basics. Again, I think what we have to think about is that a lot of our investing careers were defined by very non normal monetary policy, right? Why were central banks created? They were created to keep inflation from becoming this runaway challenge. But price stability in the context of the Fed's mandate has actually meant,
turns.zh: 我认为最后那两个因素其实很重要，我稍后会回来讲。但先说基本盘。我们还是得承认：我们大部分投资生涯是被非常态的货币政策定义的。央行为什么而生？是为了防止通胀变成失控的麻烦。但在美联储任务语境下，价格稳定实际上意味着：

turns.en: hey, we don't have high enough prices, we don't have enough inflation, and we need to create policies that actually push inflation up. Today, this Fed is very different, it's trying to pull inflation back down. And I'm sure I'm saying the obvious, right? Everyone feels the pints of inflation, we go to the gas price, we go to the grocery store, we go out to dinner, right?
turns.zh: 价格不够高、通胀不够多，我们需要制定能把通胀推上去的政策。而今天的这个美联储完全不同，它在努力打压通胀。我知道这是明摆着的事，对吧？人人都感受到通胀的切肤之痛：去看油价、去超市、出去吃饭，都是那种让人瞠目结舌的'什么情况，这什么时候发生的？'

turns.en: It's that eye popping. What the heck? When did this happen? And so I think really the first thing that I would say is this Fed is different. And I think that we are all grappling with questions around inflation and a question whether or not the Fed actually has what it takes to get inflation and keep inflation under control. Thankfully, we haven't had a runaway challenge with inflation. We certainly haven't had a significant reason to
turns.zh: 所以我要说的第一点是：这个美联储不一样了。我想我们大家都在与通胀问题角力，也都在问美联储到底有没有本事把通胀控制住。值得庆幸的是，通胀还没失控，我们也并没有重大的理由去……

turns.en: believe the Fed isn't serious. But gosh, worse coming in so far has been a different Fed chair. And I think the first thing that I would say is high rates might actually be good for bringing the long end down, because it really should give investors the belief that we will keep inflation around 2%, which means now we just have to price growth on top of that uncertainty on top of that. And I think that's actually the biggest catalyst is we
turns.zh: ……相信美联储不够认真。但天哪，Warsh上任以来，带来的已经是一位不同的美联储主席。我想说的第一点是：高利率其实可能有助于把长端利率打下来，因为它应该能让投资者相信我们会把通胀保持在2%左右。那样的话，我们只需要在此基础上再对增长和不确定性定价。我认为这才是最大的催化剂——

turns.en: just need to see demand come down a little bit, hopefully avoid the actual slowdown and get inflation under control. But the second thing that I would say is again, what are rates, what are high rates supposed to do? They're supposed to make the cost of doing things, the cost of capex, the cost of consumption that much higher, which means we're supposed to have less of it. In short, it's not a medicine that most of us like to take, but
turns.zh: 第二点还是那句话：高利率本来就该干什么？它就该让做事的成本、资本开支（capex）的成本、消费的成本都高得多，从而让我们少做少花。简单说，这不是我们大多数人爱吃的药，但它本来就是要抑制需求。这么做的时候，你希望过程漂亮有序，

turns.en: it's supposed to suppress demand. And so when you do that, you hope to do it in a nice and orderly way. But there's always the risk that it doesn't work out that way. And so honestly, I think that the big rise in rates here, it's causing some challenges around the world. There are probably levered players that are feeling it, there are banks that maybe are in a little bit less good shape. When you see big moves, you
turns.zh: 但风险在于事情未必如此。所以坦白说，我认为这次利率大幅上行已经在全球造成了一些挑战。加杠杆的参与者多半感受到了压力，有些银行的状况可能也不太妙。看到大幅波动时，你就不得不担心这些跳跃式事件。所以对我来说，这是一种有趣的保险——

turns.en: have to worry about these jump events. And so to me, it's an interesting form of insurance, because the risks of something unexpected happening have certainly risen. The other thing, of course, if we end the war, and the Middle East, probably oil prices would come down, there's just a whole lot of catalysts that are building up. And we don't have that crystal ball, we don't know the timing. But as the teeter
turns.zh: 因为意料之外事情发生的风险确实上升了。另一件事当然是，如果中东战争结束，油价大概率会回落。催化剂正在大量累积，只是我们没有水晶球，不知道时点。但当摇摇欲坠开始晃动的时候，我们就得想一想超出基准情形的事情可能发生什么，

turns.en: totter begins to move, we have to think about what may happen that isn't our base case. But do we have the portfolio built to withstand that as well? And again, I think fixed income is a really interesting ballast to some of those potential risks.
turns.zh: 而我们的组合是否也做好了抵御的准备？同样，我认为固收是应对这些潜在风险的非常好的压舱石。

turns.en: You mentioned the Fed and Chairman Kevin Warsh earlier. How do you think they're handling everything? Do you think they're doing enough to bring inflation back to the 2% target? And clearly, they have a very difficult balancing act here because they don't want to kill economic growth. I think they are apolitical, but you could make the case, there's some political concerns, but considerations will say, how do
turns.zh: 你之前提到了美联储和主席Kevin Warsh。你觉得他们处理得怎么样？为把通胀拉回2%的目标，他们做得够吗？显然这是一个非常艰难的平衡，因为他们不想扼杀经济增长。我相信他们是超党派的，但也可以说存在一些政治上的顾虑和考量。那么，你觉得美联储处理得怎么样？你觉得他们对吗？

turns.en: you think the Fed is handling everything? Do you think they're handling this correctly? Well, look, I think anyone that wants to look at their boss would would say I might do things a little bit differently.
turns.zh: 这个，我想任何人看看自己的老板，都会说我可能会把某些事情做得不太一样。

turns.en: But in general, yeah, I do. I really, really do. And so the first thing I want to say a couple of things on this, I think it's important if we're going to say, hey, how is the Fed doing? We first have to define what is the Fed trying to do? How am I measuring them? And to me, it's always important to go back to and I really like talking about this is the Fed actually has three mandates. We talk about two of them. We
turns.zh: 但总的来说，是的，我认可，非常认可。关于这个话题我想先说几点：要评价美联储干得如何，我们得先定义它想干什么、我用什么标尺衡量它。对我来说，永远重要的是回到这一点，而且我很喜欢谈：美联储其实有三项任务。我们常谈其中两项，

turns.en: talk about price stability and maximum employment. But if the actual congressional mandate is price stability, maximum employment and moderate long term interest rates. And to me, that moderate long term interest rates is one that we don't talk enough about, not because it's definable in any way, shape or form. Is it two? Is it five? Is it eight? I don't know what moderate long term interest rates are. But I think what
turns.zh: 价格稳定和充分就业——但国会给它的实际任务其实是价格稳定、充分就业和温和的长期利率（moderate long term interest rates）。而'温和的长期利率'这条，我认为我们谈得太少了——不是因为它可以以任何形式定义。是2？是5？是8？我也不知道什么叫温和的长期利率。但我认为美联储做的，

turns.en: the Fed does is they define that as kind of flexibility on which one of those goals they focus on more when they're kind of not in unison. And really, to answer your question more directly, I think Kevin Warsh is saying, I took over the Fed, and I have an inflation challenge, I need to bring it back down. But more so than that, we've been above trend inflation for far too long, investors have been patient. And
turns.zh: 是把这一项理解为一种灵活度：当几个目标不一致时，更聚焦于哪一个。更直接地回答你的问题：我觉得Kevin Warsh在说的是——我接手美联储，面临一个通胀挑战，得把它打下来。更进一步说，通胀高于趋势已经太久了，投资者一直很耐心。而我担心终有一天，

turns.en: I worry that eventually, they're not going to believe that we have what it takes to get back to 2%. And so I like to talk about that third mandate as as meaning inflation's expectation stability. And so I think we've already answered a question to some degree, you're right, coming in Kevin Warsh, there is some political independence questions. And I think those to me are out the door. We have to remind ourselves the second
turns.zh: 他们不再相信我们有能力回到2%。所以我把第三项任务理解为通胀预期的稳定。我想我们已经某种程度上回答了问题：你说得对，Kevin Warsh上任时确实存在政治独立性的疑问，但在我看来，这些疑虑已经可以放下了。我们要记得第二次记者会，对吧？

turns.en: press conference, right? Chairman Warsh shows up, they didn't raise rates. And he said, Hey, we didn't raise rates today, and you think maybe nothing happened. But gosh, a lot happened underneath the surface volatility is high rates are dramatically higher. And that's a good thing. And so to me, the Fed is doing what it needs to do with showing its credibility, it's raising rates in the face of sustained higher inflation. And
turns.zh: Warsh主席出席，没有加息。他说：我们今天没有加息，你可能以为什么都没发生。但天哪，水面之下发生了很多——波动率很高，利率大幅走高。而这是好事。所以在我看来，美联储正在做它该做的事以展示可信度：面对持续偏高的通胀，它在维持高利率，

turns.en: it's willing to take the pain of potentially less demand. I'll say one more just very quick thing to me, that transition, right, we'll just stay with the two mandates price stability, maximum employment, I think Powell, he took over a Fed where you've worried a lot more about a lack of demand and the employment side. And so I think his balancing was, yes, I want to get inflation under control, but I really want to make sure I
turns.zh: 而且愿意承受需求可能减少的痛苦。再快速说一句：说到那个过渡——只谈价格稳定和充分就业这两项任务——我认为Powell接手的美联储，更让人担心的是需求不足和就业端。所以他的平衡是：我确实想把通胀控制住，但我更想确保不削弱劳动力市场。

turns.en: don't weaken the labor market. Warsh took over a very different environment, inflation had been high, he didn't have to make that transition. And so I think he's focusing on the other one.
turns.zh: Warsh接手的是一个完全不同的环境，通胀已经很高，他不需要做那种过渡。所以我认为他聚焦的是另一头：

turns.en: I'm willing to take a little bit of pain on the employment side, no, I don't want a lot, but I'm willing to take a little bit. But gosh, we really have to get inflation back to 2%. And so just that is a subtle and nuanced point. But I think it's incredibly important. I think it's the right thing here.
turns.zh: 在就业端愿意承受一点痛苦——不，我不想要太多，但愿意承受一点。但天哪，我们真的必须把通胀拉回2%。就是个微妙而细腻的点，但我认为它极其重要，我认为这个方向是对的。

turns.en: Just a few minutes left here. You mentioned potential pain on the economic side. We haven't spent much time talking about the credit side of the equation, we've been focusing on duration risk. And again, I was looking this morning, credit spreads have ticked up recently, though they're still low on a relative basis. But just very briefly, anything standing out to you on the credit side specifically?
turns.zh: 只剩几分钟了。你提到经济端可能的痛苦。我们还没怎么聊信用这一侧，一直在讲久期风险。今天早上我看了看，信用利差最近有所走阔，但相对水平仍然很低。很简短地问：单看信用这边，有什么特别让你关注的吗？

turns.en: Well, I think the biggest thing that is standing out is you're seeing the weaker companies in particular, right, the triple C part of that high yield market, the lowest of the low, I guess, if you will, experience real stress. And so that's exactly what typically happens in a slowing economy. It tends to be a leading indicator of potential challenges. It doesn't necessarily mean like, hey, run for the hills and hide under a
turns.zh: 我认为最显眼的是较弱的那些公司，尤其是高收益市场里的triple C那一档——最低的那批——正在承受真正的压力。这正是经济放缓时通常会出现的情形，往往是潜在麻烦的先行指标。它不一定意味着大家赶紧逃命、躲到石头底下，

turns.en: rock. It just means that we really need to have our ears perked up. But across the board, what I would say is I've been surprised quite honestly, I think we all have that how well the economy has been able to handle higher rates, how well the economy has been able to handle higher inflation, higher oil prices, a housing shock, all sorts of things. underlying companies are an incredibly strong spot. But what we found
turns.zh: 它只是提醒我们真要竖起耳朵。但整体而言，坦白说，我一直很惊讶——我想我们都一样——经济承受高利率的能力居然这么强，扛住高通胀、高油价、房地产冲击等各种事情的能力也这么强，底层公司依然是非常结实的一环。但我们发现的是：

turns.en: ourselves with is we've had a very accommodative Fed, I think that is ending, we've had companies continue to expand margins, I question how much more they can expand. And we've had a consumer that has the ability to just continue spending, regardless of their own deterioration of the balance sheet. And I think all of those forces are now colliding where credit spreads to me, we have to be cautious. There are some
turns.zh: 我们一直有非常宽松的美联储，我觉得这正在结束；公司一直在扩张利润率，我怀疑还能再扩张多少；消费者不管自己的资产负债表在恶化，仍继续花钱。我觉得所有这些力量正在相撞。所以信用利差方面，我认为我们必须要谨慎。有一些很有意思的机会：

turns.en: really interesting opportunities, data centers very interesting within that the non agency mortgage space, there's tremendous opportunities. But it's something we're watching very closely.
turns.zh: 数据中心非常值得关注；非机构按揭（non agency mortgage）领域也有很多巨大的机会。但这是我们正在密切观察的事情。

turns.en: Before I let you go, if we attempt to sort of pull everything we've covered together here between the ETFs and how you're viewing fixed income markets, we talked duration risk credit risk. What would be your parting words to investors as they evaluate their fixed income positioning?
turns.zh: 放你走之前，如果我们试着把今天谈的所有东西串起来——从ETF到你怎么看固收市场，聊了久期风险、信用风险——当投资者评估自己的固收配置时，你想送给他们的临别之言是什么？最重要的是什么？

turns.en: Like what do you think is the most important moving forward? Yeah, to me, the most important thing is to recognize again, go back to basics. Why do you own a fixed income portfolio? Why may you want to own a fixed income portfolio? What is it meant to do? And do you have a manager in place and a solution in place that you think actually is additive to your portfolio? And so I think that the way that I would really summarize the
turns.zh: 对我来说，最重要的还是回到基本面：你为什么持有一个固收组合？你可能为什么需要固收组合？它是用来干什么的？你选的经理和解决方案，是不是真的对你的组合有增益？所以，如果我要真正总结这场对话的话，就是：ETF是投资者产品阵列里很好的补充，

turns.en: conversation is ETFs are a great addition to an investor's lineup, right? They give that daily liquidity, immediate ability to trade significant transparency. They're a great tool to us on the asset management side. But really, the solution is what matters most and the solution and the world of fixed income is tremendously different today.
turns.zh: 对吧？它提供每日流动性、即时可交易性、很高的透明度，对我们资管方也是很好的工具。但真正重要的是解决方案本身，而固收世界里的解决方案今天已经大为不同。

turns.en: Yields are back where they're interesting. They provide that interesting level of income. And I really do think that they can provide ballast to an investor's portfolio. But this is an incredibly important point as well, right? The world of spreads is tight. The world of risk is higher. There's a lot more uncertainty. And so I would go back to something we talked about earlier, I would focus on how do I keep an interesting
turns.zh: 收益率回来了，它们很可观，提供了不错的收入水平。我真的认为它们能够为投资者的组合提供压舱。但这一点同样极其重要：利差的世界仍然很紧，风险的世界更高，不确定性更多。所以回到我们之前谈过的，我会聚焦于如何保持一个可观的……

turns.en: level of yield, but protect on the downside and relative value to me really allows a portfolio manager to do that. Jeff, greatly enjoyed this conversation. Truly excellent perspective on the fixed income markets really appreciate that.
turns.zh: 收益水平，同时做好下行保护，而相对价值在我看来正是让组合经理做到这一点的东西。Jeff，非常享受这次对话，你对固收市场的看法真的精彩，非常感谢。

turns.en: Congratulations on the launch of the ETFs. And thank you for joining me. Yeah, thank you. It's been a great conversation. There's always so much to talk about. I appreciate it.
turns.zh: 恭喜你们发行这些ETF，也谢谢你来参加节目。是的，谢谢你。这是一次很棒的对话，总有那么多可聊的，我很感激。
